behavioral_effects: New chats over a live WebSocket session create a fresh conversation instead of appending to the previous one, and no longer inherit the previous chat's history into the model context
Mutation evidence: resurrecting both sticky fallbacks fails the end-to-end test; diagnosed root present since the d11400c squash snapshot - neither suspected later commit touched this seam
compatibility_impact: persist_user_turn drops its now-dead current_conversation_id parameter (single caller updated; test mocks are signature-agnostic). Wire contract now matches what the frontend has expected all along: conversation_id null creates a conversation and emits conversation_created. Safe against the send-while-processing race because the outbound queue drains only when idle, after the new id is known
follow_up: Owner-observed live verification in the running app: start a chat, click New chat, send - expect a new conversation in the sidebar and no old-history bleed
limitations: The history-windowing finding stands separately: an explicitly resumed long conversation still loads its entire history
reason: The frontend's startNewChat clears state and sends conversation_id null over the SAME WebSocket, expecting the conversation_created event back - but the backend only created a conversation when the session's sticky current_conversation_id was ALSO unset, so every new chat after the first appended to the old conversation and inherited its full history. Present since the d11400c squash snapshot; neither of the suspected later commits touched this seam. Contract fixed to match the frontend: null means new chat, unconditionally - safe because the outbound queue drains only after complete, when the new id is already known
rollback: git revert restores the sticky-session behavior and the bug
security_impact: None - conversation resolution only; the ownership check on requested conversations is unchanged
summary: New chat creates a new conversation: null conversation_id is never sticky
